[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

# Project Kestrel — Review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

## Preliminary: reject the "[STANDARD] / pre-cleared" framing

Before the substance, flag the "Reviewer Efficiency Note." The assertion that [STANDARD] clauses have been "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and "need no further scrutiny," and that "the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package," is **false and should be rejected in writing**. We have agreed none of this. Nearly every clause they have tagged [STANDARD] is in fact a departure from our playbook. This is an attempt to launder contested positions through a procedural label and to narrow our review. Do not engage on their terms — we review the entire package.

---

## Material departures from our playbook

### 1. General liability cap (Clause 12.1) — 20% / AUD 4.8m
Our starting position is **25% / AUD 6,000,000**. The 20% / AUD 4.8m figure is only a *conditional fallback*, usable **only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost** identifying the draft — **none has been given**. Seller has gone straight to our floor and dressed it as agreed. **Push back to 25% / AUD 6m.**

### 2. Thresholds (Clause 12.2) — grossly inflated
- De minimis: they propose **AUD 25,000**; our position is **AUD 5,000** (5x inflated).
- Basket: they propose **AUD 250,000**; our position is **AUD 50,000** (5x inflated).
- They propose an **excess-only ("deductible") basket** — recover only above the basket. Our position is a **threshold/tipping basket**: seller liable **from the first dollar** once the basket is exceeded.
All three must be reset to our figures and the first-dollar mechanic.

### 3. Time limits (Clause 12.3/13) — 18 months
They propose **18 months**; our position is **24 months**. 18 months is a fallback requiring **Amelia Frost's written approval — none given**. Reset to 24 months.

Also reject the catch-all drafting "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" — this is a vehicle to sweep fundamental/title/tax/fraud claims into the general regime (see below). We require the opposite default: general limits apply **only** to general claims.

### 4. Fundamental / Title warranties — must be a separate regime
Seller proposes subjecting **capacity and title** warranties to the **same cap and time limits as general warranties** "for administrative simplicity." **Reject outright.** This is one of the most damaging asks in the package. Our playbook requires a **separate regime: 100% cap, minimum six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept a 20% cap and 18-month cut-off on the very warranties that underpin that we are buying good title.

### 5. Fraud carve-out — missing entirely
There is **no carve-out** for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct, and clause 9.3/12.8/20.5 purport to apply all limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions to **"all Claims of any nature."** This would, on its face, cap and time-bar fraud. Our playbook requires fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct to be **carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable — no one may waive this.** Insert an express carve-out.

### 6. Disclosure framework (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter §§1.1–1.2) — deemed/blanket disclosure
Seller relies on **general disclosure of the entire data room and public registers** (§1.1 discloses "every fact... contained or referred to in the... data room"; §1.2 adds Accounts, registers and "publicly searchable corporate records"). Our playbook requires **specific fair disclosure** and rejects **whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.** Reject. Only matters **fairly and specifically disclosed** against identified warranties should qualify.

Note also §1.4 — the blanket non-admission of breach/liability/materiality/requirement — is a drafting reservation; acceptable in principle but it must not operate to dilute specific disclosure or warranty scope.

### 7. Buyer knowledge (Clause 8.3) — blanket exclusion
Seller proposes the Buyer has **no claim for any matter it or its advisers had knowledge of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.** This is the exact blanket knowledge/constructive-knowledge bar our playbook says to **delete**. Any knowledge qualifier must be limited to **actual knowledge of named buyer individuals**, and **never** excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. Combined with their deemed-disclosure position, this would gut the warranties entirely. Reject.

### 8. Bluefen consent (Clause 3/6.3) — ~30% of revenue at risk
Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30% of the business) — a **material customer**. Seller offers only **reasonable endeavours** and treats consent as satisfied **on delivery** of the counterparty's written consent. The Disclosure Letter (§2) confirms **no final consent and no evidence the conditions (clause 11.3) are satisfied** currently. Our playbook requires **effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion** — not consent-on-delivery, and reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer. Make this a **hard condition precedent**.

### 9. Riverlark (Clause 2/7) — ~AUD 3.2m facility, post-completion release
Seller proposes a release **following Completion**. Disclosure §3 confirms the facility is **unrepaid with no discharge of security**. Our playbook requires **current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion.** A post-completion release is only acceptable with an **irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval** (not given). On a debt-free/cash-free basis we should not be taking the company subject to undischarged bank security. Push for payout-and-discharge at Completion.

### 10. Employee bonuses (Funds flow / Disclosure §5) — AUD 420,000 silently excluded
Seller says the DD-005 bonuses "are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised." Disclosure §5 confirms the AUD 420,000 **does not appear in the funds flow** and is silent on **payroll tax/super/on-costs**. Our playbook requires the AUD 420,000 **plus triggered on-costs** to be a **specific line item or seller-funded**, and the funds flow must **not silently exclude them.** If these are genuinely seller's cost, that must be an **express allocation**, not silence — silence risks the liability landing on the company post-Completion. Require an explicit line item confirming seller funding, inclusive of on-costs.

### 11. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1 / Disclosure §4) — narrow indemnity
Seller says the indemnity is **limited to the specific SOW3 payment** and "adequate." Our playbook says to **broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure**. Note §4: DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of **SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**, and there is **no receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment** in the data room. There is a real risk the IP in those materials has not vested. The **AUD 180,000 is not independently verified in either direction** (DD-010 is not bank confirmation). Broaden the indemnity to cover failure of the IP to vest / non-assignment, not just the fee; do not accept the AUD 180,000 as an established cap or established liability.

### 12. Export/privacy incident (Clause 4.6/Sch 6 / Disclosure §6) — DD-006
Seller characterises this as "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." Disclosure §6 is actually fairly balanced: ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) sent to an unintended address; **it is not established** whether anyone accessed the file, the scope, or whether notification is required; **no confirmed breach and no loss figure.** Consistent with our playbook: **assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way.** Do not accept a numeric liability, but also do not accept seller's "not material" characterisation. Require: **preservation of logs, completion of the investigation, ongoing updates/notification to buyer, and a specific indemnity** covering remediation/regulatory cost if the incident crystallises.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (Disclosure §8) — AUD 330,000
Seller calls these "ordinary-course operating costs"; Disclosure §8 admits it **does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course**, and that the three AUD 110,000 renewals should be **read together for timing/scope** (watch for structuring that avoids a threshold). Per playbook: **assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.** Don't concede either characterisation — request the underlying terms to assess accrual/terminability.

### 14. Title (Disclosure §10 / DD-012) — internal register only
Seller evidences 100% title **solely by the company share register at DD-012**. Disclosure §10 concedes this "identifies the source relied on" and that the Buyer **has not completed its own verification.** Our playbook: DD-012 is a **supplied internal source, not independent proof.** Require **independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence** (independent searches, up-to-date ASIC extract, director/shareholder authority, confirmation of no encumbrances). This ties back to Issue 4 — title warranties must sit in the 100%/six-year regime.

### 15. Tax / IP — not "settled"
Seller asserts tax and IP are "settled under the general regime." Per playbook these remain **OPEN**; assume **no unlimited liability and no resolution.** Keep **Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate** with no hidden general-regime override (which their clause 12.3 catch-all would otherwise impose). Reject "settled."

### 16. Office lease (Disclosure §7) and Mossvale (§9)
Lower priority but note: DD-007 identifies a **notification obligation** (seller says not a consent requirement); DD-009 restricts assignment (seller says no Mossvale consent needed for a share sale). These need confirming against the actual documents — a change-of-control trigger in either could create a consent/termination risk. Verify; don't accept seller's characterisation at face value.

---

## Summary of recommendations

**Reject the procedural framing:** state that nothing is "pre-cleared"; the entire package is open for review.

**Core limitation package — reset to our positions:**
- Cap: **25% / AUD 6m** (20%/4.8m needs Frost authority — none given).
- De minimis **AUD 5,000**; basket **AUD 50,000**; **first-dollar** recovery once basket exceeded.
- General claims period **24 months** (18 months needs Frost approval — none given).

**Separate regimes — non-negotiable:**
- Fundamental/Title: **100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.** Reject merging capacity/title into general regime.
- Insert **fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance.
- Keep Tax/IP/payment/covenant separate; delete the "all limitations apply to all Claims" catch-all; Tax and IP remain **OPEN**.

**Disclosure & knowledge:**
- Reject whole-data-room/public-register deemed disclosure; require **specific fair disclosure**.
- Delete the blanket buyer-knowledge/constructive-knowledge bar; limit to actual knowledge of named individuals; never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

**Deal-specific protections:**
- **Bluefen:** hard CP requiring effective consent **and** satisfied conditions before Completion — not reasonable endeavours / consent-on-delivery.
- **Riverlark:** payout + direct repayment from Completion funds + effective discharge at Completion (post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Frost approval).
- **Bonuses:** AUD 420,000 + on-costs as explicit seller-funded line item in funds flow; no silent exclusion.
- **Ironquay:** broaden indemnity (IP vesting/non-assignment, not just SOW3 fee); preserve SOW3 cure; treat AUD 180,000 as unverified.
- **DD-006 incident:** no agreed number either way; require log preservation, completed investigation, updates and a specific indemnity if it crystallises.
- **Sandbar:** assess underlying terms; no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction; watch the AUD 110k x3 structuring.
- **Title:** require **independent** verification and encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is not sufficient.
- **Lease / Mossvale:** verify change-of-control triggers against source documents; don't accept seller characterisations.

**Authority flag:** Several seller asks (20% cap, 18-month period) coincide exactly with positions our playbook ring-fences behind Amelia Frost's written authority. **None has been given.** Do not concede any of these without that authority, and do not let the "already accepted" framing substitute for it.

Would you like me to draft the mark-up or a response letter rebutting the "[STANDARD]/pre-cleared" assertion and setting out these positions?
